1	# 可組合技能層級架構設計：Atoms → Molecules → Compounds
2	
3	**日期：** 2026-04-27
4	**來源：** Shiv Sakhuja (@shivsakhuja) — [X Article](https://x.com/shivsakhuja/status/2047124337191444844), 2026-04-23
5	**參考實作：** [gooseworks-ai/goose-skills](https://github.com/gooseworks-ai/goose-skills) (475★, 108 skills)
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 背景
10	
11	### 現行 Agent Skills 標準的限制
12	
13	Anthropic 的 Agent Skills 開放標準採用**扁平結構**——每個 skill 都是對等的資料夾，內含 `SKILL.md` 和可選資源。這在 skill 數量少時運作良好，但隨著規模擴大會出現問題：
14	
15	- **Skill 爆炸**：100+ 個扁平 skill 全部競爭 context window
16	- **缺乏組合性**：skill 之間沒有正式的呼叫/依賴關係
17	- **重複勞動**：每個複合工作流都得從頭寫，無法複用原子能力
18	
19	### 深度 Skill Graph 為什麼行不通
20	
21	直覺上，讓 skill 任意互相呼叫（像 Obsidian 知識圖譜一樣）似乎很自然。但 Shiv 的實務經驗指出，當依賴深度增加時，這種「自由圖」模式會崩壞：
22	
23	| 失敗模式 | 說明 |
24	|---|---|
25	| **非確定性累積** | 每個節點都是 agent 的決策點，錯誤機率隨深度指數增長 |
26	| **執行深度不確定** | Agent 無法預知 chain 會走多深 |
27	| **循環依賴風險** | A → B → C → A 形成死循環 |
28	| **判斷力過度委託** | 每一跳都把「該不該呼叫」的決定權交給 agent |
29	
30	單層 `Skill A → Skill B` 通常沒問題。問題出在**深度 ≥ 3 和密度高**的圖。
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 核心提案：三層組合模型
35	
36	將深度限制在**恰好三層**，用化學隱喻命名：
37	
38	```
39	Compounds（化合物）  ← 人類操作層
40	    ↓ 編排 8-10 個
41	Molecules（分子）    ← 顯式工作流層
42	    ↓ 串接 2-10 個
43	Atoms（原子）        ← 原始能力層
44	```
45	
46	### 第一層：Atoms（原子）= Capabilities
47	
48	**定義：** 單一用途、窄範圍、不可再分的原始技能。
49	
50	**特性：**
51	
52	| 屬性 | 要求 |
53	|---|---|
54	| 職責 | 做好一件事 |
55	| 可靠性 | 接近確定性（近乎 100% 成功率） |
56	| 是否呼叫其他 skill | **否** — 原子是葉節點 |
57	| 輸入/輸出 | 明確定義，可預測 |
58	| 失敗處理 | 快速失敗，錯誤訊息清晰 |
59	
60	**範例：**
61	
62	| Atom | 做什麼 |
63	|---|---|
64	| `scrape-linkedin-profile` | 抓取一個 LinkedIn 個人頁面 |
65	| `find-person-on-apollo` | 用 Apollo API 找一個人 |
66	| `verify-email-hunter` | 用 Hunter.io 驗證 email |
67	| `review-pr` | 審查一個 Pull Request |
68	| `blog-feed-monitor` | 透過 RSS 抓取部落格更新 |
69	| `meta-ad-scraper` | 抓取 Meta 廣告素材 |
70	
71	**設計原則：**
72	- 原子**永遠不呼叫其他 skill** — 這是最核心的約束
73	- 如果一個 atom 需要拆分，它就不是 atom
74	- 原子是可被任何 molecule 複用的積木
75	
76	---
77	
78	### 第二層：Molecules（分子）= Composites
79	
80	**定義：** 中層技能，透過串接 2–10 個 atoms 來解決一個有明確邊界的問題。
81	
82	**特性：**
83	
84	| 屬性 | 要求 |
85	|---|---|
86	| 職責 | 解決一個有界問題（bounded problem） |
87	| 組合方式 | **顯式的** — 分子本身宣告何時、如何呼叫哪些 atom |
88	| Agent 判斷空間 | 最小化 — 組合邏輯寫死在 SKILL.md 裡，不是 runtime 決定 |
89	| Atom 數量 | 2–10 個 |
90	| 是否呼叫其他 molecule | **否** — 分子不呼叫分子 |
91	
92	**關鍵洞察：組合邏輯下沉到 skill 本身**
93	
94	傳統做法是讓 agent 在 runtime 決定「接下來該呼叫哪個 skill」。Molecule 模式的核心區別是：**組合邏輯被推入分子的 SKILL.md 中**。Agent 不需要判斷——它照著 SKILL.md 的步驟走。
95	
96	```markdown
97	# lead-qualification（分子）
98	
99	## 步驟
100	
101	1. 呼叫 `find-person-on-apollo` — 取得候選人清單
102	2. 呼叫 `verify-email-hunter` — 驗證每個人的 email
103	3. 根據 ICP 標準打分
104	4. 輸出合格名單到 CSV
105	
106	## 原子依賴
107	- find-person-on-apollo
108	- verify-email-hunter
109	```
110	
111	**分子的兩種形態：**
112	
113	| 形態 | 說明 | 適用場景 |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| **嚴格序列** | Atom A → B → C → D，固定順序 | 流程明確、無分支 |
116	| **有限編排** | 小型 orchestrator，有少量判斷邏輯 | 需要簡單條件分支（如「如果 email 無效就跳過」） |
117	
118	**範例：**
119	
120	| Molecule | 串接的 Atoms | 做什麼 |
121	|---|---|---|
122	| `competitor-intel` | reddit + twitter + linkedin + blog scrapers | 綜合競爭情報 |
123	| `lead-qualification` | find leads → verify → score | 線索驗證與評分 |
124	| `leadership-change-outreach` | detect → evaluate → enrich → draft | 高管變動偵測+外聯 |
125	
126	---
127	
128	### 第三層：Compounds（化合物）= Playbooks
129	
130	**定義：** 高層編排器，運行多個 molecules 完成端到端的業務流程。
131	
132	**特性：**
133	
134	| 屬性 | 要求 |
135	|---|---|
136	| 職責 | 端到端工作流 |
137	| Agent 自主性 | **高** — 這是 agent 獲得真正自主權的層級 |
138	| 確定性 | 先天較低 — 因為跨多個分子的編排涉及更多判斷 |
139	| 人類角色 | 今天仍需人類駕駛（human driver） |
140	| Molecule 數量 | 推薦上限 8–10 個 |
141	
142	**範例：**
143	
144	| Compound | 編排的 Molecules | 做什麼 |
145	|---|---|---|
146	| `outbound-prospecting-engine` | signal detection → research → qualify → contact → personalize → campaign | 完整外銷開發流程 |
147	| `event-prospecting-pipeline` | find attendees → research → qualify → dedup → outreach | 活動場景線索挖掘 |
148	| `feature-launch-playbook` | brief → content → graphics → distribution | 功能上線全套物料 |
149	
150	---
151	
152	## 槓桿模型：為什麼三層能放大人類產出
153	
154	核心論點是關於**人類的「大腦 RAM」**——context switching 和管理多個 agent 是真正的瓶頸。
155	
156	### 數學模型
157	
158	```
159	1 Compound ≈ 編排 ~10 Molecules
160	1 Molecule ≈ 串接 ~10 Atoms
161	─────────────────────────────────
162	1 人管理 Compounds = 撬動 ~100 個原子級任務
163	```
164	
165	### 注意力分配原則
166	
167	| 層級 | 人類注意力 | 原因 |
168	|---|---|---|
169	| Atoms | **零** | 近乎確定性，不需要監督 |
170	| Molecules | **極低** | 顯式工作流，失敗時快速報錯 |
171	| Compounds | **高** | 這裡才需要人類判斷 |
172	
173	**結論：** 人類應該**只在 Compound 層級操作**。把確定性的低層工作全部交給 skill 自己處理，人類的判斷力集中在高層的「做不做」和「做什麼」。
174	
175	---
176	
177	## 可靠性邊界
178	
179	Shiv 自己承認的已知限制：
180	
181	| 邊界 | 描述 |
182	|---|---|
183	| **Compound 上限** | 單個 compound 編排超過 ~8-10 個 molecules 時，可靠性開始下降 |
184	| **跨 Compound 編排** | 目前沒有定義「Compound 的 Compound」，因為那又回到了深度圖的問題 |
185	| **Agent 判斷上限** | Compound 層級的 agent 自主性仍受限於當前模型能力 |
186	
187	---
188	
189	## 檔案結構：雙檔案契約
190	
191	每個 skill 目錄必須包含兩個檔案：
192	
193	```
194	skill-name/
195	├── SKILL.md           # Agent/人類可讀的指令文件
196	└── skill.meta.json    # 機器可讀的元資料
197	```
198	
199	### SKILL.md
200	
201	遵循 Agent Skills 開放標準的格式：
202	
203	```markdown
204	---
205	name: skill-slug
206	description: >
207	  一句話描述這個 skill 做什麼、什麼時候用。
208	license: MIT
209	compatibility: 所需的外部依賴或前置條件。
210	metadata:
211	  author: author-name
212	  version: "1.0"
213	---
214	
215	# Skill 名稱
216	
217	## 用途
218	...
219	
220	## 步驟（Molecules/Playbooks 才有）
221	1. 呼叫 `atom-a` — 做 X
222	2. 呼叫 `atom-b` — 做 Y
223	...
224	
225	## 原子依賴（Molecules 才有）
226	- atom-a
227	- atom-b
228	```
229	
230	> **注意：** 層級（tier）資訊不放在 SKILL.md frontmatter 中。Tier（`atom` / `molecule` / `compound`）由 `skill.meta.json` 的 `tier` 欄位宣告，並透過目錄結構（`atoms/`、`molecules/`、`compounds/`）體現。這讓 SKILL.md 保持為純指令文件，元資料關注點全部集中在 `skill.meta.json`。
231	
232	### skill.meta.json
233	
234	```json
235	{
236	  "slug": "skill-slug",
237	  "tier": "atom | molecule | compound",
238	  "version": "1.0.0",
239	  "description": "機器可讀的描述（可與 SKILL.md 的 description 相同）",
240	  "depends_on": ["atom-a", "atom-b"],
241	  "platform": "universal | github | gitlab",
242	  "tags": ["tag1", "tag2"],
243	  "installation": {
244	    "targets": ["opencode", "claude", "codex"],
245	    "base_path": "<tier>/<slug>"
246	  }
247	}
248	```
249	
250	> **`tier` 欄位** 是層級分類的唯一機器可讀來源。工具鏈（ds-skills validate、corgispec CLI）根據此欄位驗證依賴方向約束，並決定 skill 在目錄結構中的位置（`atoms/`、`molecules/`、`compounds/`）。
251	
252	**為什麼要雙檔案？**
253	
254	| 檔案 | 消費者 | 用途 |
255	|---|---|---|
256	| `SKILL.md` | Agent + 人類 | 執行指令、progressive disclosure |
257	| `skill.meta.json` | 工具鏈 | 安裝、驗證、索引、依賴分析 |
258	
259	`SKILL.md` 是 agent 在 runtime 讀取的東西。`skill.meta.json` 是 CLI 工具、linter、registry 在 build time 用的東西。分離兩者讓每一邊都能獨立演化。
260	
261	---
262	
263	## 層級約束規則（不可違反）
264	
265	這些是整個模型的硬性約束：
266	
267	| 規則 | 說明 |
268	|---|---|
269	| **Atom 不呼叫 Atom** | 原子是葉節點，自包含 |
270	| **Atom 不呼叫 Molecule** | 禁止向上依賴 |
271	| **Molecule 只呼叫 Atom** | 分子只能向下一層 |
272	| **Molecule 不呼叫 Molecule** | 禁止同層依賴（避免隱式深度） |
273	| **Compound 只呼叫 Molecule** | 化合物只能向下一層 |
274	| **Compound 不呼叫 Atom** | 禁止跨層（必須經過 Molecule） |
275	| **Compound 不呼叫 Compound** | 禁止同層依賴（避免回到深度圖） |
276	| **最大深度 = 3** | Compound → Molecule → Atom，不能更深 |
277	
278	```
279	✅ Compound → Molecule → Atom     （合法）
280	✅ Molecule → Atom                 （合法）
281	✅ Atom                            （合法，獨立運行）
282	❌ Compound → Atom                 （非法，跨層）
283	❌ Molecule → Molecule             （非法，同層）
284	❌ Compound → Compound             （非法，同層）
285	❌ Atom → Molecule                 （非法，向上依賴）
286	```
287	
288	---
289	
290	## 與現有模式的比較
291	
292	### vs. 扁平 Skills（Anthropic 標準）
293	
294	| 維度 | 扁平 Skills | 三層模型 |
295	|---|---|---|
296	| 結構 | 所有 skill 對等 | 嚴格三層 |
297	| 組合性 | 無正式機制 | Molecule 顯式串接 Atom |
298	| 擴展性 | Skill 數量增長 → context 壓力 | 層級索引，只載入需要的層 |
299	| 進入門檻 | 低 | 中（需要理解三層分類） |
300	| 適用規模 | < 30 skills | 30-500+ skills |
301	
302	### vs. 深度 Skill Graph
303	
304	| 維度 | 深度圖 | 三層模型 |
305	|---|---|---|
306	| 深度 | 無限制 | 硬性上限 3 |
307	| 靈活性 | 最高 | 受限但足夠 |
308	| 可靠性 | 隨深度衰減 | 可預測 |
309	| Debug 難度 | 困難（路徑不確定） | 容易（層級清晰） |
310	| 循環風險 | 高 | 零（層級約束消除循環） |
311	
312	### vs. 我們現有的 OpenSpec GitFlow Skills
313	
314	| 維度 | 現有結構 | 三層模型可能的改進 |
315	|---|---|---|
316	| 組織方式 | 按功能命名的扁平 skill 目錄 | 按層級分類 + 功能命名 |
317	| 組合方式 | Skill 內部引用其他 skill（隱式） | 顯式 `depends_on` + 層級約束 |
318	| 元資料 | YAML frontmatter 在 SKILL.md | 額外 `skill.meta.json` 分離關注點 |
319	| 安裝 | `install-skills.sh` 全量複製 | 可按需安裝特定層級 |
320	
321	---
322	
323	## 已知開放問題
324	
325	1. **Compound 的 Compound？** 當業務流程確實需要 4 層以上時怎麼辦？Shiv 沒有答案——他認為這回到了深度圖的問題，目前建議是「拆分成多個獨立 Compound，由人類手動串接」。
326	
327	2. **跨 Molecule 共享狀態** 多個 Molecule 需要共享中間結果時（如一個抓資料，另一個用同一份資料做分析），狀態傳遞機制不明確。Gooseworks 似乎用 CSV/spreadsheet 作為隱式共享介面。
328	
329	3. **動態路由** 如果一個 Compound 需要根據運行時結果決定呼叫哪個 Molecule（而不是固定序列），判斷邏輯放哪裡？目前 Compound 的 SKILL.md 本身承擔了這個角色，但沒有正式的 routing DSL。
330	
331	4. **版本相容性** Atom 升級 API 時，依賴它的 Molecules 是否自動適配？目前沒有版本約束機制。
332	
333	5. **測試策略** 如何測試 Molecule 是否正確串接 Atoms？Gooseworks 有 `validate-skills.js` 但只做結構驗證，不做行為測試。[skillkit](https://github.com/sakhilchawla/skillkit) 專案正在嘗試解決這個問題。
334	
335	---
336	
337	## 結論
338	
339	三層 Atoms → Molecules → Compounds 模型的核心洞察是：
340	
341	> **組合性不是 agent 的 runtime 判斷問題，而是 skill 的 design-time 結構問題。**
342	
343	把「什麼呼叫什麼」的決定從 agent 的 runtime 推回到 skill 作者的 design-time，就能在保持組合性的同時維持可靠性。深度限制在 3 層、每層 ~10 個下游、禁止同層和向上依賴——這些硬性約束看似限制了靈活性，但實際上消除了深度圖的全部失敗模式。
344	
345	這是一個值得認真評估的架構模式，尤其當 skill 庫規模超過 30 個時。
346

1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	## What this repo is
4	
5	A workflow/skills toolkit (not an app) that turns AI coding assistants into structured engineering workflows via Corgi. It ships skills, schemas, CLI tooling, and slash commands for Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex.
6	
7	There is no application code to build or deploy. The "product" is the skill files and their metadata.
8	
9	## Directory layout
10	
11	| Path | Role |
12	|------|------|
13	| `.opencode/skills/corgispec-*/` | **Source of truth** for skill definitions (SKILL.md + skill.meta.json) |
14	| `.opencode/commands/corgi-*.md` | OpenCode slash command dispatch |
15	| `.claude/skills/corgispec-*/` | Claude Code skill mirrors — must stay in sync with `.opencode/skills/` |
16	| `.codex/skills/corgispec-*/` | Codex skill mirrors — must stay in sync with `.opencode/skills/` |
17	| `openspec/schemas/` | Schema definitions (gitlab-tracked, github-tracked) |
18	| `openspec/config.yaml` | Project-level config (schema, isolation, context) |
19	| `schemas/skill-meta.schema.json` | JSON Schema for validating `skill.meta.json` |
20	| `packages/corgispec/` | **corgispec CLI** — unified CLI replacing ds-skills + install-skills.sh |
21	| `tools/ds-skills/` | Node CLI for skill validation + dependency graphing (legacy, use corgispec instead) |
22	| `install-skills.sh` | Installs user-level skills (legacy, use `corgispec install` instead) |

44	```
45	
46	Uses Node.js built-in test runner (`node --test`). Requires Node >= 18.
47	
48	### Other ds-skills commands
49	
50	```bash
51	node bin/ds-skills.js list --path ../..    # list all skills
52	node bin/ds-skills.js graph --path ../..   # dependency graph
53	```
54	
55	### Install skills to user level
56	
57	```bash
58	./install-skills.sh          # copies to ~/.claude/skills/ and ~/.config/opencode/skill/
59	./install-skills.sh --dry-run  # preview only
60	```
61	
62	## Skill authoring rules
63	
64	- Each skill lives in its own directory with exactly two files: `SKILL.md` (instructions) and `skill.meta.json` (metadata).
65	- `skill.meta.json` must validate against `schemas/skill-meta.schema.json`.
66	- Skill slugs are kebab-case, must match the directory name.
67	- Tier hierarchy: `atom` (no deps) -> `molecule` (depends on atoms) -> `compound` (depends on molecules/atoms).
68	- Platform field: `universal`, `github`, or `gitlab`.
69	- `corgispec-gh-*` skills are GitHub variants; unprefixed `corgispec-*` are GitLab or universal.
70	
71	## Three-directory sync obligation
72	
73	`.opencode/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, and `.codex/skills/` must contain equivalent skill content. When editing a skill, update all three directories. The `.opencode/skills/` version is canonical.
74	
75	## No CI
76	
77	There are no CI workflows. Validation is manual via `ds-skills validate` or `corgispec validate`.
78	
79	## Config
80	
81	- `openspec/config.yaml` controls which schema (`gitlab-tracked` or `github-tracked`) is active and optional worktree isolation settings.
82	- `.opencode/package.json` only declares `@opencode-ai/plugin` — this enables skill discovery in OpenCode sessions.
83	
84	## Conventions
85	
86	- Markdown skill files reference tool names generically. Platform-specific tool mapping is handled at runtime by each AI platform.
87	- The workflow is checkpoint-based: propose -> apply (one Task Group at a time) -> review -> archive.
88	- Delta specs use ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED/RENAMED operations.
89	
90	## Coding Guidelines
91	
92	Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
93	
94	> **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
95	
96	### 1. Think Before Coding
97	
98	Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.
99	
100	Before implementing:
101	- State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
102	- If multiple interpretations exist, present them — don't pick silently.
103	- If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
104	- If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
105	
106	### 2. Simplicity First
107	
108	Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.
109	
110	- No features beyond what was asked.
111	- No abstractions for single-use code.
112	- No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
113	- No error handling for impossible scenarios.
114	- If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
115	
116	Ask yourself: *"Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?"* If yes, simplify.
117	
118	### 3. Surgical Changes
119	
120	Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.
121	
122	When editing existing code:
123	- Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
124	- Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
125	- Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
126	- If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it — don't delete it.
127	
128	When your changes create orphans:
129	- Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
130	- Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
131	
132	**The test:** Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
133	
134	### 4. Goal-Driven Execution
135	
136	Define success criteria. Loop until verified.
137	
138	Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
139	- "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
140	- "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
141	- "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
142	
143	For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
144	```
145	1. [Step] → verify: [check]
146	2. [Step] → verify: [check]
147	3. [Step] → verify: [check]
148	```
149	
150	Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
151	
152	---
153	
154	*These guidelines are working if: fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.*
155	
156	## Session Memory Protocol
157	
158	### Startup (every session)
159	Read in order, max 3 files:
160	1. `memory/session-bridge.md` — last session's state
161	2. `wiki/hot.md` — current project context (~500 words, hard cap 600)
162	3. `wiki/index.md` — jump to relevant domain page
163	Then read `docs/` or code as needed.
164	
165	### Retrieval Budget
166	- Startup: max 3 files (session-bridge + hot + index), then on-demand
167	- Per-question: max 2 wiki pages before answering
168	- If >5 pages needed: say "this needs a deep session"
169	
170	### File Size Limits (hard caps)
171	| File | Target | Hard Cap | Overflow Action |
172	|------|--------|----------|-----------------|
173	| wiki/hot.md | 500 words | 600 words | Trim oldest entries |
174	| wiki/index.md | 40 lines | 80 lines | Archive completed entries |
175	| memory/pitfalls.md | 10 active | 20 active | Rotate oldest 10 |
176	| memory/session-bridge.md | 30 lines | 50 lines | Archive old Done items |
177	
178	### Shutdown (every session end)
179	Update `memory/session-bridge.md`: Done / Waiting / New Pitfalls / New Discoveries
180	
181	### corgi Apply -> Long-term Memory
182	After each Task Group completes:
183	- New pitfalls -> append to `memory/pitfalls.md` (link source change)
184	- New implicit rules -> append to `wiki/architecture/implicit-contracts.md`
185	- Update `wiki/hot.md` Recent Decisions
186	
187	### Compaction Triggers (agent self-maintains)
188	- Every archive: compress session-bridge
189	- pitfalls > 20 entries: rotate oldest 10 to Archive section
190	- hot.md > 550 words: trim oldest entries
191	- Every 10 corgi sessions: suggest running /corgi-lint
192

1	## ADDED Requirements
2	
3	### Requirement: Tier-based directory structure
4	Skill directories SHALL be organized into tier-based subdirectories (`atoms/`, `molecules/`, `compounds/`) under each platform's skills root, matching the `tier` field declared in each skill's `skill.meta.json`.
5	
6	#### Scenario: Atoms reside in atoms/ subdirectory
7	- **WHEN** a skill has `"tier": "atom"` in its skill.meta.json
8	- **THEN** the skill directory is located at `<skills-root>/atoms/<skill-name>/`
9	- **THEN** this applies to all platform directories (`.opencode/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.codex/skills/`, `packages/corgispec/assets/skills/`)
10	
11	#### Scenario: Molecules reside in molecules/ subdirectory
12	- **WHEN** a skill has `"tier": "molecule"` in its skill.meta.json
13	- **THEN** the skill directory is located at `<skills-root>/molecules/<skill-name>/`
14	
15	#### Scenario: Compounds reside in compounds/ subdirectory
16	- **WHEN** a skill has `"tier": "compound"` in its skill.meta.json
17	- **THEN** the skill directory is located at `<skills-root>/compounds/<skill-name>/`
18	
19	### Requirement: base_path includes tier prefix
20	The `base_path` field in `skill.meta.json` SHALL include the tier subdirectory prefix, reflecting the actual filesystem location relative to the skills root.
21	
22	#### Scenario: Atom base_path has atoms/ prefix
23	- **WHEN** `corgispec-memory-init` (atom) has its base_path read
24	- **THEN** the value is `"atoms/corgispec-memory-init"`
25	
26	#### Scenario: Molecule base_path has molecules/ prefix
27	- **WHEN** `corgispec-propose` (molecule) has its base_path read
28	- **THEN** the value is `"molecules/corgispec-propose"`
29	
30	### Requirement: Codex symlinks reflect tier structure
31	The `.codex/skills/` symlinks SHALL point to the tier-prefixed paths in `.claude/skills/`, maintaining the same tier-based directory layout.
32	
33	#### Scenario: Codex symlinks resolve through tier subdirectories
34	- **WHEN** Codex reads `atoms/corgispec-memory-init/SKILL.md` via `.codex/skills/`
35	- **THEN** the resolved path is `.claude/skills/atoms/corgispec-memory-init/SKILL.md`

38	The `discoverSkills()` function SHALL discover skills by scanning tier subdirectories first, falling back to flat root only when tier directories do not exist.

41	- **WHEN** `discoverSkills()` scans a skills root with `atoms/` and `molecules/` subdirectories
42	- **THEN** all skills in those subdirectories are discovered

51	- **THEN** no `type` field appears in the example
52	- **THEN** a note explains that tier information is conveyed via `skill.meta.json`'s `tier` field

1	# OPSX Verify Stage and Routing Accuracy Upgrade Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-04-22
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Introduce a first-class `verify` stage into the OPSX workflow and improve routing accuracy without replacing the existing command-wrapper plus platform-skill architecture.
8	
9	The target shape is:
10	
11	`propose -> apply -> verify -> review -> advance/repair -> archive`
12	
13	This design also defines how to borrow the strongest parts of `agent-skills`—explicit routing discipline, preflight classification, and failure-to-route rules—without changing OPSX into a free-form intent router.
14	
15	## Scope
16	
17	This design covers:
18	
19	- separating evidence collection from human review decisions
20	- introducing `/corgi-verify` and `/corgi:verify`
21	- defining local canonical `verify` state and report outputs
22	- improving command routing accuracy with explicit routing rules
23	- formalizing browser-aware verification for UI-facing work
24	- phasing rollout from local-only verify to optional tracker-visible verify
25	
26	This design does **not** cover:
27	
28	- replacing shallow command wrappers with a generic orchestration engine
29	- collapsing review approval into automation
30	- introducing a mandatory tracker-visible `verify` state in phase 1
31	- building a full Chrome DevTools-style runtime inspection system in the first iteration
32	
33	## Context
34	
35	Current OPSX workflow documentation and skill surfaces already expose the key seam this design builds on:
36	
37	- `apply` ends after implementation, closeout, tracker sync, and review handoff
38	- `review` currently mixes evidence gathering, quality checks, human decision prompting, and state mutation
39	- GitLab review is already partly decomposed into evidence, decisions, and repair references
40	- GitHub review is still more monolithic
41	- UI verification already exists in scattered form via Playwright screenshot capture, screenshot evidence requirements, and Playwright planning templates
42	
43	The repository's existing design direction already favors:
44	
45	- shallow wrappers
46	- authoritative local state
47	- explicit human gates
48	- replayable side-effect phases
49	
50	This proposal extends that direction instead of replacing it.
51	
52	## Problem Statement
53	
54	Today, OPSX review does too much.
55	
56	It acts as both:
57	
58	1. the place where evidence is collected and quality checks are run, and
59	2. the place where a human is asked to approve, reject, or discuss the result and where workflow state is mutated
60	
61	This creates three concrete problems:
62	
63	1. **Boundary blur** — evidence collection and decision-making are coupled in one command surface.
64	2. **Routing ambiguity** — wrappers and platform skills must infer too much from partially prepared state.
65	3. **UI verification fragmentation** — Playwright and screenshot evidence exist, but only as embedded review or planning instructions instead of a first-class phase.
66	
67	## Design Summary
68	
69	The recommended design is a staged architecture:
70	
71	- **Target architecture:** `apply -> verify -> review -> advance/repair`
72	- **Phase 1 rollout:** local-only `verify` phase, no tracker-visible `verify` label required
73	- **Phase 2 option:** add tracker-visible `verify` state if the local-only phase proves stable and valuable
74	
75	This design intentionally separates:
76	
77	- **core work** from **quality verification**
78	- **quality verification** from **human decision**
79	- **human decision** from **tracker mutation**
80	
81	## Updated Phase Contract
82	
83	### Apply
84	
85	Purpose: execute one task group and close it out locally and in tracker mirrors.
86	
87	- **Owns:** discover, develop, closeout
88	- **Produces:** task-group outputs, closeout summary, canonical handoff state, tracker mirror update
89	- **Must not do:** perform final quality verification or ask for approve/reject/discuss
90	- **Ends with:** verify handoff, not review handoff
91	
92	### Verify
93	
94	Purpose: gather evidence, run checks, and produce a verify report.
95	
96	- **Owns:** evidence collection, build/test/lint validation, UI/browser verification when required, verify report generation
97	- **Reads:** closeout state, changed files, evidence references, tracker context if needed
98	- **Writes:** verify report, verify status in canonical local state, evidence references
99	- **Must not do:** ask for approval, reject the work as a workflow decision, or mutate progression state beyond verify status
100	
101	### Review
102	
103	Purpose: consume the verify report and run the explicit human decision gate.
104	
105	- **Owns:** approve / reject / discuss prompt, review note/report consumption, advance/repair transition
106	- **Reads:** verify report, canonical local state, review comments, acceptance discussion
107	- **Writes:** approved transitions only, plus any repair-ready state on rejection
108	- **Must not do:** own primary evidence gathering as a normal path
109	
110	### Advance / Repair
111	
112	Purpose: apply the explicit human decision.
113	
114	- **Approve:** move forward toward merge/archive readiness
115	- **Reject:** create or point to repair-ready follow-up state
116	- **Discuss:** remain review-blocked pending more input
117	
118	## Routing Accuracy Upgrade
119	
120	OPSX should borrow routing discipline from `agent-skills`, but not its intent-first architecture.
121	
122	The key borrow is **decision discipline**, not free-form command selection.
123	
124	### 1. Router Contract
125	
126	Add one repo-level routing contract that defines, for each command surface:
127	
128	- valid entry conditions
129	- required prior artifacts/state
130	- forbidden conditions
131	- expected outputs
132	- failure conditions that must stop the flow instead of guessing
133	
134	This becomes the authoritative routing reference across wrappers and platform skills.
135	
136	### 2. Preflight Classification
137	
138	Before dispatch, each wrapper should classify the current request against a shared checklist:
139	
140	- target change / task group identity
141	- current canonical local phase
142	- tracker state compatibility
143	- required handoff artifact presence
144	- whether the change is UI-facing and therefore browser evidence-sensitive
145	
146	This classification is read-only. It should not perform substantive work.
147	
148	### 3. Negative Routing Rules
149	
150	Add explicit stop conditions so the system fails clearly instead of improvising.
151	
152	Examples:
153	
154	- `review` must fail if no verify report exists
155	- `verify` must fail if apply closeout is incomplete
156	- `review` must fail if the target is still in active implementation state
157	- `verify` must fail UI-related work when required browser evidence is missing
158	- `review` must not silently collect missing core evidence except as a narrow recovery path
159	
160	These rules are the highest-value routing upgrade because they reduce false progression.
161	
162	## Browser-Aware Verification
163	
164	This design separates **browser-aware verification** from **browser-debug tooling**.
165	
166	### Phase 1: Browser-Aware Verify
167	
168	In phase 1, `verify` gains first-class support for UI-facing validation using the patterns already present in the repo:
169	
170	- Playwright screenshot capture
171	- UI evidence blocks
172	- screenshot artifact upload patterns
173	- Playwright sprint planning documents
174	
175	When verify detects UI-facing changes, it should require browser evidence such as:
176	
177	- key screenshots
178	- relevant Playwright run output
179	- minimal UI flow confirmation for changed surfaces
180	- any required artifact links in the verify report
181	
182	### Phase 2: Browser-Debug Capability
183	
184	In phase 2, OPSX may add a dedicated browser-debug or browser-verify capability inspired by `agent-skills/browser-testing-with-devtools`.
185	
186	This later capability may include:
187	
188	- console inspection
189	- network inspection
190	- runtime DOM/state checks
191	- richer browser debugging workflows
192	
193	This is deliberately out of MVP scope because the repo currently has evidence patterns for Playwright and screenshots, but not an established DevTools-style inspection model.
194	
195	## Canonical Local State Additions
196	
197	Phase 1 should extend canonical local state with verify metadata.
198	
199	Minimum additions:
200	
201	```yaml
202	phase: verify
203	verify:
204	  status: pending | passed | failed | needs-input
205	  report_path: <path to verify report>
206	  ui_evidence_required: true | false
207	  ui_evidence_present: true | false
208	  last_verified_at: <timestamp>
209	```
210	
211	This keeps repo-local state authoritative while allowing tracker mirrors to lag behind until a later upgrade.
212	
213	## Tracker Strategy
214	
215	### Phase 1 Recommendation: Local-Only Verify
216	
217	The first implementation should **not** require a tracker-visible `verify` label/state.
218	
219	Reasons:
220	
221	- lower migration risk across GitLab and GitHub flows
222	- fewer changes to issue sync and review selection logic
223	- preserves current public workflow while improving internal correctness
224	- fits the repository's stated preference for authoritative local state
225	
226	### Phase 2 Option: Tracker-Visible Verify
227	
228	If phase 1 proves stable, phase 2 may add tracker-visible `verify`.
229	
230	That would require updating:
231	
232	- issue sync references and label transitions
233	- wrapper expectations
234	- README workflow text and diagrams
235	- review selection logic for both platforms
236	
237	This should be treated as a deliberate second-stage migration, not bundled into the first delivery.
238	
239	## Wrapper Responsibilities
240	
241	Wrappers remain shallow.
242	
243	### `/corgi-apply` / `/corgi:apply`
244	
245	- preserve config and isolation checks
246	- dispatch by schema
247	- verify postconditions around one-group execution and closeout
248	- end with verify handoff expectations instead of review handoff expectations
249	
250	### `/corgi-verify` / `/corgi:verify`
251	
252	- preserve config and isolation checks
253	- dispatch by schema
254	- enforce verify preconditions
255	- verify postconditions such as: verify report exists, required evidence exists, UI evidence exists when required
256	
257	### `/corgi-review` / `/corgi:review`
258	
259	- preserve config and isolation checks
260	- require verify report existence before proceeding
261	- enforce explicit human decision gate
262	- verify postconditions around decision prompt and approved transition handling
263	
264	## Browser Evidence Contract
265	
266	For UI-facing work, verify should produce a consistent evidence packet.
267	
268	Minimum expected contents:
269	
270	- changed UI surfaces or routes covered
271	- command(s) used for browser verification
272	- screenshot references or artifact links
273	- pass/fail status for required UI checks
274	- notes on gaps, flaky behavior, or missing environment prerequisites
275	
276	This contract should be reused by review and by any later browser-debug capability.
277	
278	## Rollout Plan
279	
280	### Phase 1 — Introduce Verify Locally
281	
282	- add verify wrappers
283	- split evidence/checks out of review
284	- keep review as human gate + advance/repair
285	- add local canonical verify metadata
286	- add browser-aware verify for UI changes
287	- add router contract, preflight classification, and negative routing rules
288	
289	### Phase 2 — Promote Verify Across Tracker Surfaces
290	
291	- add optional tracker-visible verify label/state
292	- update sync logic and public docs
293	- align review consumer logic to start after verify instead of after apply
294	
295	### Phase 3 — Expand Browser Debugging
296	
297	- add richer browser-debug tooling if needed
298	- formalize console/network/runtime inspection flows
299	- keep this as a separate capability from basic browser-aware verify
300	
301	## Acceptance Criteria
302	
303	- OPSX workflow is documented as `apply -> verify -> review -> advance/repair`
304	- verify is explicitly evidence-only and review is explicitly decision-only
305	- wrappers remain shallow and schema-driven
306	- local canonical state includes verify metadata
307	- review fails clearly when verify prerequisites are missing
308	- UI-facing changes require browser evidence during verify
309	- GitLab and GitHub platform skills follow the same conceptual phase boundaries even where implementation details differ
310	- the design preserves explicit human control over progression decisions
311	
312	## Non-Goals
313	
314	- making review fully automatic
315	- introducing a generic workflow engine
316	- forcing tracker-visible verify in the first rollout
317	- bundling full browser-debug instrumentation into MVP
318	
319	## Why This Design
320	
321	This design takes the strongest verified patterns already present in the repository—closeout evidence, Playwright-backed UI review, screenshot artifacts, and explicit human gates—and reorganizes them into cleaner boundaries.
322	
323	It also borrows the most useful part of `agent-skills`: not its global free-form intent routing, but its insistence on explicit applicability rules, lifecycle discipline, and refusal to proceed when prerequisites are missing.
324	
325	The result is a workflow that is stricter, easier to reason about, and better aligned with the repository's existing architectural direction.
326

1	# Unified Router Workflow Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-04-21
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Define one stable workflow architecture for `propose`, `apply`, and `review` that keeps command wrappers shallow, separates core work from tracker synchronization, preserves explicit human decision points, and reduces drift between GitLab and GitHub flows.
8	
9	## Scope
10	
11	This design covers workflow shape, phase boundaries, handoff rules, failure isolation, and refactor order.
12	
13	This design does **not** propose a generic workflow engine, new infrastructure, or a full rewrite of the existing command-wrapper plus platform-skill structure.
14	
15	## Context
16	
17	Based on the current repository:
18	
19	- `propose` is already close to a shallow router, with a DAG shaped like `proposal -> {spec, design} -> tasks`.
20	- `apply` wrappers are already shallow routers, but platform skills still mix execution, summary generation, tracker sync, and verification.
21	- GitLab `review` is partially decomposed into worktree discovery, quality checks, review decisions, and repair flow.
22	- GitHub `review` is still comparatively monolithic.
23	- Tracking metadata currently drifts between what `propose` writes and what `apply` reads.
24	- The repo already contains a stronger split in the GitLab issue-phase flow: development, finishing/closeout, reviewing, and merging.
25	
26	## Design Principles
27	
28	1. Keep the existing **command wrapper -> platform skill** architecture.
29	2. Make **repo-local state authoritative**; tracker state mirrors it.
30	3. Split **core work** from **tracker mutation**.
31	4. Require explicit human gates for promotion decisions.
32	5. Make side-effect phases replayable without rerunning core work.
33	6. Fix boundary drift before introducing broader abstractions.
34	
35	## Shared Phase Contract
36	
37	All three workflows use the same phase vocabulary:
38	
39	### 1. Discover
40	
41	Purpose: resolve target, context, worktree, prior outputs, and current tracker state.
42	
43	- **Reads:** config, schema, worktree state, canonical local metadata, prior outputs, tracker state
44	- **Writes:** nothing persistent
45	- **Must not do:** generate new substantive outputs or change workflow state
46	
47	### 2. Develop
48	
49	Purpose: produce the primary local outputs for the current workflow.
50	
51	- **Reads:** canonical inputs from `discover`
52	- **Writes:** primary local outputs only
53	- **Must not do:** mutate tracker state or infer approval
54	
55	### 3. Closeout
56	
57	Purpose: package results, update canonical handoff state, and mirror status to the tracker.
58	
59	- **Reads:** primary outputs plus current tracker state
60	- **Writes:** canonical handoff/status record, tracker comments/links/labels/status mirrors
61	- **Must not do:** create new substantive work or reinterpret workflow intent
62	
63	### 4. Review
64	
65	Purpose: collect evidence, run checks, and prepare a decision packet.
66	
67	- **Reads:** outputs, evidence, closeout state, tracker context if needed
68	- **Writes:** findings and a decision packet only
69	- **Must not do:** promote workflow state by itself
70	
71	### 5. Advance / Repair
72	
73	Purpose: apply an explicit human decision.
74	
75	- **Reads:** decision packet plus explicit user choice
76	- **Writes:** approved transitions only, such as apply-ready, accepted, back-to-repair, merge-ready, closed, or archived
77	- **Must not do:** guess human intent from prior comments, labels, or passing checks
78	
79	## Workflow Mapping
80	
81	### Propose
82	
83	- **Discover:** resolve config, schema, worktree, existing change state, existing tracker state, and source context
84	- **Develop:** generate `proposal -> {spec, design} -> tasks`
85	- **Closeout:** write canonical handoff/status state and create or update tracker mirrors
86	- **Review:** present the proposal/spec/tasks package for human review
87	- **Advance:** mark the package apply-ready only after approval
88	
89	### Apply
90	
91	- **Discover:** resolve worktree, change, target task group, canonical handoff state, and tracker references
92	- **Develop:** execute one task group and produce local evidence
93	- **Closeout:** write execution summary, update canonical status, and sync child/parent tracker state
94	- **Review:** prepare a review packet for that task group
95	- **Advance / Repair:** move into review or return to repair based on explicit decision
96	
97	### Review
98	
99	- **Discover:** resolve target group, worktree, canonical state, tracker context, and prior evidence
100	- **Review:** run checks, gather findings, and prepare a decision packet
101	- **Advance:** apply human approval, rejection, or discussion outcome to tracker and canonical state
102	- **Repair:** on rejection, generate repair-ready follow-up state without rerunning evidence collection unless needed
103	
104	## Canonical Handoff / Status Record
105	
106	The design requires one canonical local handoff/status record per tracked workflow subject.
107	
108	This record is the source of truth between phases. It must carry enough information for the next phase to resume without reconstructing meaning from tracker comments or labels.
109	
110	At minimum, it must identify:
111	
112	- stable target identity
113	- current workflow phase
114	- primary output locations or references
115	- tracker references
116	- pending or resolved decision state
117	- last successful closeout/sync point
118	
119	This design does not require a new service. It only requires one normalized local contract that `propose` writes and `apply` / `review` consume.
120	
121	## Authority and Invariants
122	
123	1. **Local canonical state is authoritative.** GitLab or GitHub state mirrors local state and must not replace it.
124	2. **Later phases resume from persisted outputs.** No phase may depend on scraping tracker comments or labels to reconstruct core outputs.
125	3. **Closeout is replayable.** If tracker sync fails after local work succeeds, rerun `closeout`, not `develop`.
126	4. **Advance is decision-driven.** No state promotion without an explicit user choice.
127	5. **Review does not mutate progression by itself.** Checks may recommend, but they do not approve.
128	
129	## Human Gates
130	
131	The following transitions require explicit human confirmation:
132	
133	- proposal package -> apply-ready
134	- review packet -> accept vs reject vs discuss
135	- merge / close / archive transitions
136	
137	Mirror-only sync does not require a new human gate, but it also must not invent one.
138	
139	## Failure Isolation
140	
141	The architecture is designed so that failures stop inside the smallest possible phase.
142	
143	### If `develop` succeeds and `closeout` fails
144	
145	Primary outputs remain valid. Retry `closeout` only.
146	
147	### If `review` succeeds and `advance` is not approved
148	
149	Evidence remains valid. Wait for human choice without changing progression state.
150	
151	### If tracker APIs fail
152	
153	Canonical local state remains usable. Tracker sync is delayed, not treated as core output loss.
154	
155	### If tracker and local state disagree
156	
157	Local canonical state wins. Closeout replays the tracker mirror.
158	
159	## Refactor Blueprint
160	
161	### Keep
162	
163	- shallow command wrappers as platform routers
164	- current `propose` DAG for `proposal -> {spec, design} -> tasks`
165	- GitLab review decomposition shape as the baseline review skeleton
166	
167	### Split
168	
169	#### Apply
170	
171	Split platform apply skills into:
172	
173	- **core executor** for one task group
174	- **tracker-sync finalizer** for summary and child/parent issue updates
175	- **review packet handoff** for the next phase
176	
177	#### Review
178	
179	Split review into:
180	
181	- **evidence collector**
182	- **decision gate**
183	- **mutation executor**
184	- **repair handler**
185	
186	#### Propose
187	
188	Keep the current artifact DAG, but end it in `closeout` instead of treating tracker creation as part of the primary output itself.
189	
190	### Align
191	
192	- GitHub review must align to the same phase contract already visible in GitLab review.
193	- Tracker schema must be normalized so that `propose` and `apply` agree on the same local metadata contract.
194	
195	## Minimum Viable Refactor Order
196	
197	### 1. Normalize tracker schema
198	
199	Fix the `propose` writer / `apply` reader boundary first. This removes the most dangerous current drift.
200	
201	### 2. Split apply into `develop` and `closeout`
202	
203	This creates immediate stability gains because execution can succeed independently from tracker synchronization.
204	
205	### 3. Align GitHub review to the GitLab review skeleton
206	
207	Bring GitHub review to the same phase model: discover, review, advance/repair.
208	
209	### 4. Upgrade propose into a complete phase-based router
210	
211	Do this last, because propose is already closest to the target shape.
212	
213	## Out of Scope
214	
215	- a generic workflow engine
216	- replacing command wrappers with a new orchestration layer
217	- collapsing human gates into automation
218	- hiding real GitHub/GitLab platform differences behind premature abstraction
219	
220	## Why This Design
221	
222	This design reuses the strongest pattern already proven in the repo: the GitLab split between development, closeout, review, and merge. It fixes the most dangerous boundary first, preserves explicit human control, and improves retry behavior without forcing a framework rewrite.
223

3	description: Automated verification gate between apply and review — runs tests, checks spec coverage, validates lint/build. No human gate required.

10	---
11	
12	Run automated verification on a completed Task Group before review. Verify assures the code works; review judges if it's good enough.
13	
14	## Preconditions (VERIFY BEFORE STARTING)
15	
16	- [ ] Change exists in `openspec/changes/<name>/`
17	- [ ] If tracked: `.gitlab.yaml` or `.github.yaml` exists with group issue numbers
18	- [ ] If `isolation.mode` is `worktree`: worktree exists for this change (error if not)
19	- [ ] At least one Task Group has all tasks complete (verify needs something to check)
20	
21	## Forbidden Actions
22	
23	- NEVER ask for human input — verify is fully automated
24	- NEVER implement fixes — flag issues, do not resolve them
25	- NEVER create or close issues — only post a report note to existing child issues
26	- NEVER change issue labels or workflow state
27	- NEVER fabricate test results or evidence
28	- NEVER add Playwright/UI screenshots (those belong in review, not verify)
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Steps
33	
34	### 1. Discover: select change and resolve worktree
35	
36	**Context Gate**: If session context already contains ALL of: `isolation.mode`, active changes with worktree paths, current branch
37	→ Gate passed — SKIP config reading below and proceed to the next step.
38	Otherwise: read `openspec/config.yaml` and proceed with discovery.
39	
40	**If `isolation.mode: worktree`**: Changes live inside worktrees. Read `references/worktree-discovery.md` for the full discovery procedure. Quick summary:
41	1. `openspec list --json`, if it returns changes, use them
42	2. If empty: scan `<isolation.root>/` directories, verify each with `git worktree list` and check `openspec/changes/<name>/` exists inside
43	3. Auto-select if one found, prompt if multiple
44	4. ALL subsequent work uses the worktree as workdir
45	
46	**If no isolation**: `openspec list --json` directly. Auto-select if one, prompt if multiple.
47	
48	If name provided by user, use it directly.
49	
50	### 2. Discover: select completed Task Group
51	
52	Parse `tasks.md` to find all Task Groups (`## N.` headings). Identify which groups have ALL tasks marked `[x]`. These are the completed groups eligible for verification.
53	
54	If tracked: read the tracking file (`.gitlab.yaml` / `.github.yaml`) for group names and issue numbers.
55	
56	Default to the first completed group that hasn't been verified yet. If no completed groups exist, guidance: "No completed groups found. Run `/corgi-apply` first."
57	
58	### 3. Automated Test Execution
59	
60	Detect the project's test infrastructure and run the test suite. All detection is best-effort — skip gracefully if nothing is found.
61	
62	Use the detection table in `references/verification-steps.md` for detailed detection conditions and commands. Summary:
63	
64	| Detection Condition | Run Command | Failure Handling |
65	|---------------------|-------------|-----------------|
66	| `tests/` + `pytest.ini` / `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.pytest]` | `python -m pytest -v` | If tests fail → mark 🟡 Important, do NOT block |
67	| `package.json` with `"test"` script | `npm test` | Same as above |
68	| `bun test` exists or `bunfig.toml` | `bun test` | Same as above |
69	| `go.mod` + `_test.go` files | `go test ./...` | Same as above |
70	| No test infrastructure | Report "No test infrastructure detected", mark ⚠️, do not block |
71	
72	**Test result handling**:
73	- All tests pass → ✅ output captured, continue
74	- Some tests fail → capture failure output, mark 🟡 Important, continue
75	- No test infrastructure → mark ⚠️, note in report, continue
76	
77	Tests are evidence. Failure is a signal, not a gate.
78	
79	### 4. Spec Coverage Verification
80	
81	Compare the change's spec requirements against the actual implementation.
82	
83	Steps:
84	1. Read the spec file(s) from `openspec/changes/<name>/specs/<capability>/spec.md`
85	2. If no spec exists: note "No spec found for this group", mark ℹ️, skip
86	3. For each Requirement in the spec, check:
87	   - Is there corresponding implementation code that fulfills this requirement?
88	   - Do the Scenario behaviors map to actual code paths?
89	4. Classify each requirement:
90	   - **✅ Full**: Implementation covers all scenarios with evidence (specific file:function references)
91	   - **⚠️ Partial**: Some scenarios covered, some missing or untestable
92	   - **❌ Missing**: No implementation found for this requirement
93	
94	Output format follows the spec in `references/verification-steps.md`.
95	
96	### 5. Lint / Build Verification
97	
98	Check for project-level lint and build configuration. Run what's available.
99	
100	**Lint detection**:
101	| Condition | Command |
102	|-----------|---------|
103	| `.ruff.toml` or `[tool.ruff]` in `pyproject.toml` | `ruff check` |
104	| `.eslintrc.*` or `eslint` in `package.json` | `npx eslint .` (or configured path) |
105	| `tsconfig.json` | `npx tsc --noEmit` |
106	| No linter found | Skip, mark ℹ️ |
107	
108	**Build detection**:
109	| Condition | Command |
110	|-----------|---------|
111	| `package.json` with `"build"` script | `npm run build` |
112	| `Makefile` with `build` target | `make build` |
113	| No build config | Skip, mark ℹ️ |
114	
115	**Result handling**:
116	- Lint/build passes → ✅ captured, continue
117	- Lint/build fails → capture output, mark 🟡 Important, continue
118	- No config found → mark ℹ️, note, continue
119	
120	### 6. Generate Verify Report
121	
122	Assemble all verification results into a structured report. Read `references/verification-steps.md` for detailed report composition guidance.
123	
124	Report format (for terminal display and issue posting):
125	
126	```markdown
127	## Verify Report: Group N, {group name}
128	
129	### Test Results
130	✅ 12 passed / ❌ 0 failed / ⚠️ 2 skipped
131	
132	<test output or "No test infrastructure detected">
133	
134	### Spec Coverage
135	| Requirement | Coverage | Evidence |
136	|-------------|----------|----------|
137	| REQ-1: User login | ✅ Full | Implemented in auth/login.py:login() |
138	| REQ-2: Error handling | ⚠️ Partial | Happy path covered, null input not handled |
139	| REQ-3: Rate limiting | ❌ Missing | No rate limiting found in codebase |
140	
141	**Summary**: ✅ 2/3 fully covered | ⚠️ 1 partial | ❌ 0 missing
142	
143	### Lint / Build
144	✅ ruff: no errors | ✅ Build: success
145	
146	### Verdict
147	✅ **PASS** — Ready for review
148	```
149	
150	#### Verdict Determination
151	
152	- **✅ PASS**: All detectable checks passed (tests pass, spec fully covered, lint clean, build successful)
153	- **⚠️ PASS WITH WARNINGS**: Some checks have warnings (partial spec coverage, test failures, lint warnings) — not blocking, but noted
154	- **❌ FAIL**: Critical issues found that MUST be fixed before review (e.g., build broken, zero spec coverage for core requirements, security red flags from security checklist)
155	
156	### 7. Gate Decision and Next-Steps Guidance
157	
158	Based on the verdict from Step 6:
159	
160	**If ✅ PASS or ⚠️ PASS WITH WARNINGS**:
161	- Post the verify report to the child issue (if tracked):
162	  - GitLab: `glab issue note <child_iid> --message "$VERIFY_REPORT"`
163	  - GitHub: `gh issue comment <child_number> --body "$VERIFY_REPORT"`
164	- Print guidance: `Run /corgi-review to review this group.`
165	- If warnings present, also print: `N warnings were found. They are noted in the report but do not block review.`
166	
167	**If ❌ FAIL**:
168	- Post the verify report to the child issue (if tracked)
169	- Print guidance: `N critical issues found. Fix these before review. Run /corgi-apply to address them.`
170	- List the specific failure items for the user
171	
172	**Verify cannot replace review**. Verify proves the code works. Review judges if the code is good enough. The human gate in review is always required after verify passes.
173	
174	## Guardrails
175	
176	- Verify is fully automated — no human gate, no confirmation dialogs
177	- Evidence gathering is best-effort — skip gracefully if detection fails
178	- Test/lint/build failures are signals, not gates (except build failure = FAIL)
179	- Verify never implements fixes, changes labels, or creates/close issues
180	- Verify posts only a report note to the existing child issue (if tracked)
181	- Platform detection: read `openspec/config.yaml` schema field, use `glab` for gitlab-tracked, `gh` for github-tracked
182	- If no tracking file exists: produce the report to terminal only, no issue posting
183	- If no completed groups found: stop with guidance, do not proceed
184	
185	## Postconditions (VERIFY BEFORE REPORTING DONE)
186	
187	- [ ] Change discovered and selected
188	- [ ] Completed Task Group identified
189	- [ ] Tests executed (or gracefully skipped with note)
190	- [ ] Spec coverage assessed (or gracefully skipped if no spec)
191	- [ ] Lint/build checked (or gracefully skipped if no config)
192	- [ ] Verify report generated with explicit verdict
193	- [ ] Report posted to child issue (if tracked)
194	- [ ] Next-steps guidance printed for user
195	
196	**If you reached postconditions without producing an explicit PASS/PASS WITH WARNINGS/FAIL verdict, you violated the contract. Stop and determine the verdict.**
197

12	Review a completed Task Group with quality checks and interactive approval.
13	
14	## Preconditions (VERIFY BEFORE STARTING)
15	
16	- [ ] Change exists in `openspec/changes/<name>/`
17	- [ ] `.gitlab.yaml` exists with parent and group issue IIDs
18	- [ ] If `isolation.mode` is `worktree`: worktree exists for this change (error if not)
19	
20	## Forbidden Actions
21	
22	- NEVER auto-approve or auto-reject, ONLY the user decides
23	- NEVER change issue labels without explicit user choice
24	- NEVER close issues — closing removes them from board label columns; label changes are sufficient
25	- NEVER skip the user decision prompt in Step 5
26	- NEVER fabricate test results or screenshots
27	- NEVER implement fixes during review
28	
29	---
30	
31	## Steps
32	
33	### 1. Discover: select change and resolve worktree
34	
35	**Context Gate**: If session context already contains ALL of: `isolation.mode`, active changes with worktree paths, current branch
36	→ Gate passed — SKIP config reading below and proceed to the next step.
37	Otherwise: read `openspec/config.yaml` and proceed with discovery.
38	
39	**If `isolation.mode: worktree`**: Changes live inside worktrees, not the main checkout. Read `references/worktree-discovery.md` for the full discovery procedure. Quick summary:
40	1. `openspec list --json`, if it returns changes, use them
41	2. If empty (new session from main checkout): scan `<isolation.root>/` directories, verify each with `git worktree list` and check `openspec/changes/<name>/` exists inside
42	3. Auto-select if one found, prompt if multiple
43	4. ALL subsequent work uses the worktree as workdir
44	
45	**If no isolation**: `openspec list --json` directly. Auto-select if one, prompt if multiple.
46	
47	If name provided by user, use it directly.
48	
49	### 2. Discover: select Task Group and verify completion
50	
51	Read `.gitlab.yaml` for the group list. Check each group's labels via GitLab. Default to the first group in `workflow::review` state.
52	
53	Read `tasks.md`. If the selected group's tasks are not all `[x]`, stop.
54	
55	### 3. Review: inspect existing GitLab feedback
56	
57	Read child issue notes. If reviewer feedback exists, present it to the user before proceeding.
58	
59	### 4. Review: gather evidence and post the review report
60	
61	Run automated quality checks and assemble a Review Report.
62	
63	Quality checks inform the decision. They do not decide the outcome.
64	
65	Read `references/quality-checks.md` for the full quality check procedure (code quality, spec verification, functional testing, report format).
66	
67	Post the review report to the GitLab child issue:
68	
69	```bash
70	glab issue note <child_iid> --message "$REVIEW_REPORT"
71	```
72	
73	Posting the report records evidence for the human gate. Do not change labels, close issues, update parent progress, or generate repair tasks in this step.
74	
75	### 5. Human gate: ask the user for a decision
76	
77	**This step is MANDATORY. You MUST stop here and wait for user input.**
78	
79	Use the structured question/choice tool (e.g., `question()`) to present exactly these options.
80	Do NOT present them as plain text — use the interactive selection tool so the user can click/select directly:
81	
82	1. **Approve** — commit & push all changes, move the group issue to done, and advance
83	2. **Reject** — fail this group and enter repair (no commit)
84	3. **Discuss** — talk before deciding
85	
86	Quality checks inform the decision. Only the user approves or rejects.
87	
88	**Do NOT proceed until the user explicitly chooses.**
89	
90	### 6. Advance / Repair: execute the user's decision
91	
92	Read `references/review-decisions.md` for the full approve, reject, and discuss procedures.
93	
94	- **Approve**: commit & push local changes, move the child issue to done, update parent progress
95	- **Reject**: enter repair flow (see `references/repair-flow.md`)
96	- **Discuss**: free-form conversation, then re-ask approve or reject
97	
98	All label changes, parent updates, and repair task generation happen only inside the approve or reject paths after the user chooses.
99	
100	---
101	
102	## Postconditions (VERIFY BEFORE REPORTING DONE)
103	
104	- [ ] Review report was posted to the GitLab child issue
105	- [ ] User explicitly chose approve, reject, or discuss (not auto-decided)
106	- [ ] If approve: all local changes committed and pushed before label change (or confirmed no changes to commit)
107	- [ ] If approve: if commit or push failed, label change was NOT performed and error was reported
108	- [ ] If approve: child issue label changed to `workflow::done` (issue left open — closing removes it from board)
109	- [ ] If approve: parent issue progress updated
110	- [ ] If reject: fix tasks added to `tasks.md`, child issue moved to `workflow::in-progress`
111	- [ ] If reject: no fixes were implemented during review
112	
113	**If you reached postconditions without asking the user in Step 5, you violated the contract. Stop and re-do Step 5.**

22	- NEVER skip worktree creation when `isolation.mode` is `worktree`

24	- NEVER copy `context`, `rules`, or `project_context` blocks into artifact files
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Steps
29	
30	### 1. Discover: Get change name
31	
32	If user provided a clear name or description, derive a kebab-case name (e.g., "add user auth" → `add-user-auth`). If unclear, ask the user what they want to build.
33	
34	### 2. Discover: Resolve isolation and create worktree
35	
36	**Context Gate**: If session context already contains ALL of: `isolation.mode`, active changes with worktree paths, current branch
37	→ Gate passed — SKIP config reading below and proceed to the next step.
38	Otherwise: read `openspec/config.yaml` and proceed with discovery.
39	
40	If NOT available, read `openspec/config.yaml` and check `isolation.mode`:
41	
42	**If `isolation.mode` is `worktree`:**
43	```bash
44	git worktree add <isolation.root>/<name> -b <isolation.branch_prefix><name>
45	```
46	- Default root: `.worktrees`, default prefix: `feat/`
47	- If worktree already exists, reuse it
48	- Announce: `Worktree created at <path> (branch: <branch>)`
49	- **ALL subsequent steps use this worktree as workdir**
50	
51	**If `isolation.mode` is `none` or `isolation` section is missing:**
52	- Work in the current directory. Skip worktree steps.
53	
54	### 3. Develop: Create change directory and build artifacts in dependency order
55	
56	```bash
57	openspec new change "<name>"
58	```
59	If `openspec/changes/<name>/` already exists, reuse it.
60	
61	```bash
62	openspec status --change "<name>" --json
63	```
64	Loop through artifacts until all `applyRequires` are `done`. For each `ready` artifact:
65	```bash
66	openspec instructions <artifact-id> --change "<name>" --json
67	```
68	Use the `template` as structure, `instruction` as guidance. `context` and `rules` are constraints for YOU — never include them in output files.
69	
70	Read `references/artifact-creation.md` for detailed artifact creation procedure.
71	
72	The primary output of propose is the completed planning artifact package: `proposal -> {spec, design} -> tasks`.
73	
74	### 4. Closeout: Show final status and prepare handoff state
75	
76	```bash
77	openspec status --change "<name>"
78	```
79	
80	After the artifacts are complete, prepare the local handoff state that later phases consume. The planning artifact package remains the primary output; tracker setup and worktree metadata are closeout work layered on top of it.
81	
82	### 5. Closeout: Create issue tracking
83	
84	Read `references/gitlab-issues.md` for the full GitLab issue creation procedure.
85	
86	Skip if `.gitlab.yaml` already exists or `glab` is unavailable.
87	
88	If created, `.gitlab.yaml` is the canonical local tracking state for GitLab-tracked handoff. Later phases should consume that local state and mirror it to the platform tracker rather than treating issue creation as part of the artifact package itself.
89	
90	### 6. Closeout: Save worktree metadata (if isolation active)
91	
92	If worktree was created in Step 2, write `.worktree.yaml` in the change directory:
93	```yaml
94	path: <isolation.root>/<name>
95	branch: <isolation.branch_prefix><name>
96	created: <ISO-8601-timestamp>
97	```

99	---
100	
101	## Output

104	- Change name and location
105	- Artifacts created

108	- Worktree status: path and branch, or "none"
109	- Next step: "Review the proposal/spec/design/tasks package, then run `/corgi-apply` to start implementation."
110

1	# Verify: Verification Steps and Procedures
2	
3	Use this procedure during the verify phase, after the change and group are selected.
4	
5	These steps are fully automated. No human gate is required. All detection is best-effort — skip gracefully if the expected infrastructure is not found.
6	
7	## 1. Test Execution Procedures
8	
9	### Detection and Execution Matrix
10	
11	| Detection Condition | Framework | Execute Command | Failure Handling |
12	|---------------------|-----------|----------------|-----------------|
13	| `tests/` directory + `pytest.ini` or `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.pytest]` | pytest | `python -m pytest -v` | Failures → 🟡 Important, do not block |
14	| `package.json` with `"test"` script | npm | `npm test` | Failures → 🟡 Important, do not block |
15	| `bunfig.toml` or `bun.lockb` + test scripts | bun | `bun test` | Failures → 🟡 Important, do not block |
16	| `go.mod` + `*_test.go` files | Go | `go test ./...` | Failures → 🟡 Important, do not block |
17	| `Cargo.toml` + `#[test]` | Rust | `cargo test` | Failures → 🟡 Important, do not block |
18	| `Makefile` with `test` target | Make | `make test` | Failures → 🟡 Important, do not block |
19	| None of the above | — | Report "No test infrastructure detected" | Mark ⚠️, do not block |
20	
21	### Detection Procedure (by priority)
22	
23	1. **Check for pytest infrastructure**: Look for `tests/` directory. Check for `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml` (with `[tool.pytest]` section), or `setup.cfg` (with `[tool:pytest]`). If found, run `python -m pytest -v`.
24	2. **Check for npm/bun**: Look for `package.json`. If it has a `"test"` script, run `npm test`. If `bunfig.toml` or `bun.lockb` exists, prefer `bun test`.
25	3. **Check for Go**: Look for `go.mod`. If found and `*_test.go` files exist, run `go test ./...`.
26	4. **Check for Rust**: Look for `Cargo.toml`. If found, run `cargo test`.
27	5. **Check for Make**: Look for `Makefile`. If it has a `test` target, run `make test`.
28	6. **Fallback**: If none detected, note "No test infrastructure detected".
29	
30	### Test Result Capture
31	
32	- Capture the FULL output (stdout + stderr) of the test command
33	- Extract key metrics: total tests, passed, failed, skipped, errors
34	- Format: `✅ N passed / ❌ N failed / ⚠️ N skipped`
35	- If the command itself fails to execute (not a test failure — an infra error like "pytest not found"): report the error message and continue. Mark ℹ️.
36	
37	## 2. Spec Coverage Verification Procedure
38	
39	### Locating the Spec
40	
41	1. Read the change's spec from `openspec/changes/<name>/specs/<capability>/spec.md`
42	2. If multiple capability specs exist, read ALL of them
43	3. If no specs exist at all: report "No spec found for this group", mark ℹ️, skip the rest of this section
44	
45	### Requirement-by-Requirement Analysis
46	
47	For each requirement in the spec (look for `## Requirements` section, then individual `### REQ-*` entries):
48	
49	1. **Extract**: Requirement ID, description, and Scenario blocks (WHEN/THEN statements)
50	2. **Search**: For each scenario, search the implementation files for corresponding logic
51	   - Look in files produced by the group (from the apply Rich Summary)
52	   - Also check the broader codebase if the spec references existing modules
53	3. **Classify**:
54	   - **✅ Full**: ALL scenarios for this requirement have corresponding implementation code. Provide specific file:function references as evidence.
55	   - **⚠️ Partial**: Some scenarios covered, some missing or untestable. Note which scenarios are uncovered.
56	   - **❌ Missing**: No implementation found for ANY scenario of this requirement.
57	
58	### Coverage Calculation
59	
60	- Count requirements: total, fully covered, partially covered, missing
61	- Coverage rate = fully covered / total × 100%
62	- Report in format: `✅ N/N fully covered | ⚠️ N partial | ❌ N missing`
63	- Partially and missing requirements → each marked with appropriate severity:
64	  - Missing: 🟡 Important (spec says it should exist, but doesn't)
65	  - Partial: 🔵 Suggestion (most cases covered, minor gaps)
66	
67	## 3. Lint / Build Verification Procedures
68	
69	### Lint Detection
70	
71	| Condition | Linter | Command | Notes |
72	|-----------|--------|---------|-------|
73	| `.ruff.toml` or `[tool.ruff]` in `pyproject.toml` | ruff | `ruff check` | Python linter, very common |
74	| `.eslintrc.*` (any format) or `"eslintConfig"` in `package.json` | ESLint | `npx eslint .` | JS/TS linter |
75	| `tsconfig.json` | TypeScript | `npx tsc --noEmit` | Type check only, no emit |
76	| `.flake8` or `[tool.flake8]` | flake8 | `flake8 .` | Legacy Python linter |
77	| `.golangci.yml` | golangci-lint | `golangci-lint run` | Go linter |
78	| None detected | — | Skip | Mark ℹ️ |
79	
80	### Build Detection
81	
82	| Condition | Build System | Command | Notes |
83	|-----------|-------------|---------|-------|
84	| `package.json` with `"build"` script | npm | `npm run build` | Common in JS/TS projects |
85	| `pyproject.toml` with `[build-system]` | pip/setuptools | `python -m build` | Python package build |
86	| `Makefile` with `build` target | Make | `make build` | Generic build |
87	| `go.mod` (main package) | Go | `go build ./...` | Build without test files |
88	| None detected | — | Skip | Mark ℹ️ |
89	
90	### Result Handling
91	
92	- **Lint passes**: ✅ captured, continue
93	- **Lint warnings**: capture warning summary, mark 🟡 Important, continue
94	- **Lint errors**: capture error summary, mark 🟡 Important, continue (does not block)
95	- **Build fails**: capture error output, mark ❌ FAIL (build failure is critical — verify verdict = FAIL)
96	- **No config detected**: mark ℹ️, note in report, continue
97	
98	### Output Format
99	
100	For the verify report, present lint/build results as:
101	
102	```
103	### Lint / Build
104	✅ ruff: no errors | ✅ Build: success
105	(or)
106	⚠️ eslint: 3 warnings | ⚠️ No build config found
107	(or)
108	❌ Build: FAILED — dependency resolution error
109	```
110	
111	## 4. Report Composition
112	
113	### Assembling the Verify Report
114	
115	After all evidence is gathered (Sections 1-3 above), assemble the final verify report following this structure:
116	
117	```markdown
118	## Verify Report: Group N, {group name}
119	
120	### Test Results
121	✅ N passed / ❌ N failed / ⚠️ N skipped
122	
123	<test output or "No test infrastructure detected">
124	
125	### Spec Coverage
126	| Requirement | Coverage | Evidence |
127	|-------------|----------|----------|
128	| REQ-1: name | ✅ Full | Implemented in path/file.py:funcName() |
129	| REQ-2: name | ⚠️ Partial | Happy path covered in path/file.py. Missing: edge case X |
130	| REQ-3: name | ❌ Missing | No implementation found in codebase |
131	
132	**Summary**: ✅ N/N fully covered | ⚠️ N partial | ❌ N missing
133	
134	### Lint / Build
135	✅ ruff: no errors | ✅ Build: success
136	
137	### Verdict
138	{✅ PASS | ⚠️ PASS WITH WARNINGS | ❌ FAIL} — {next-steps guidance}
139	```
140	
141	### Verdict Logic
142	
143	Determine verdict based on accumulated results:
144	
145	- **✅ PASS**: All detected checks pass —
146	  - Tests: all passing (or no test infra → skip)
147	  - Spec coverage: all requirements fully covered (or no spec → skip)
148	  - Lint: no errors or no linter config
149	  - Build: no errors or no build config
150	  - No 🟡 Important or 🔴 Critical severity items found
151	
152	- **⚠️ PASS WITH WARNINGS**: Non-blocking issues found —
153	  - Test failures (individual test failures, not infra failure)
154	  - Partial or missing spec coverage
155	  - Lint warnings or errors (not build failures)
156	  - Any 🟡 Important items present
157	  - Guidance: "N warnings found. These are noted in the report but do not block review."
158	
159	- **❌ FAIL**: Critical issues that must block review —
160	  - Build failure (cannot verify non-building code)
161	  - 🔴 Critical security concerns detected (from security checklist if used)
162	  - Core spec requirements completely missing (not just partial)
163	  - Any issue that makes the code fundamentally untestable
164	  - Guidance: "N critical issues found. Fix these before review. Run /corgi-apply to address them."
165	
166	### Post-Report Actions
167	
168	1. If tracking file exists (`.gitlab.yaml` / `.github.yaml`):
169	   - GitLab: `glab issue note <child_iid> --message "$VERIFY_REPORT"`
170	   - GitHub: `gh issue comment <child_number> --body "$VERIFY_REPORT"`
171	2. If no tracking file: display the report in terminal only
172	3. Print the next-steps guidance based on verdict
173	4. NEVER change labels, close issues, or create new issues

1	# Worktree Discovery
2	
3	When `isolation.mode` is `worktree`, changes live inside worktrees — NOT in the main checkout. A new session starting from the main checkout cannot see them via `openspec list`.
4	
5	## Discovery Procedure
6	
7	When resolving a change with worktree isolation:
8	
9	### 1. Try normal resolution first
10	
11	```bash
12	openspec list --json
13	```
14	
15	If this returns changes, use them directly. (This works when already inside a worktree.)
16	
17	### 2. If empty — scan worktree directories
18	
19	Read `isolation.root` from `openspec/config.yaml` (default: `.worktrees`).
20	
21	```bash
22	ls <isolation.root>/
23	```
24	
25	Each subdirectory name is a potential change name. For each:
26	- Verify the worktree is registered: check `git worktree list` includes this path
27	- Verify change exists inside: check `<isolation.root>/<name>/openspec/changes/<name>/` is a directory
28	
29	### 3. Build discovered change list
30	
31	For each valid worktree change found:
32	```
33	Change: <name>
34	  Worktree: <isolation.root>/<name>
35	  Branch: <isolation.branch_prefix><name>
36	```
37	
38	### 4. Select change
39	
40	- If user specified a name: use it, verify it's in the list
41	- If only one change found: auto-select
42	- If multiple found: present the list and ask the user
43	
44	### 5. Switch to worktree
45	
46	Once selected, ALL subsequent commands run with workdir set to the absolute worktree path:
47	```
48	<project-root>/<isolation.root>/<name>
49	```
50	
51	## Example
52	
53	```
54	# Main checkout: /home/user/myproject
55	# Config: isolation.root: .worktrees, branch_prefix: feat/
56	
57	$ ls .worktrees/
58	add-user-auth    fix-login-bug
59	
60	# Verify:
61	$ git worktree list
62	/home/user/myproject                          abc1234 [main]
63	/home/user/myproject/.worktrees/add-user-auth def5678 [feat/add-user-auth]
64	/home/user/myproject/.worktrees/fix-login-bug ghi9012 [feat/fix-login-bug]
65	
66	# Check changes exist:
67	$ ls .worktrees/add-user-auth/openspec/changes/
68	add-user-auth/
69	
70	# → Valid change: "add-user-auth" at .worktrees/add-user-auth
71	```
72	
73	## When This Applies
74	
75	This discovery is needed by:
76	- **apply** — to find which change to implement
77	- **review** — to find which change to review
78	- **archive** — to find which change to archive
79	- **explore** — to investigate a change's context
80	
81	Always use this procedure when `isolation.mode: worktree` and starting from the main checkout.
82

1	# Review: Quality Checks and Evidence Gathering
2	
3	Use this procedure during the review phase, after the group is selected and before the human gate.
4	
5	These checks gather evidence for the review report. They inform the user's decision, but they do not decide the outcome.
6	
7	Do not change labels, close issues, update parent progress, or append repair tasks here.
8	
9	## 0. Anti-Rationalization Guard (READ FIRST)
10	
11	Before executing any quality checks, the agent MUST read and confirm the following anti-rationalization table.
12	If any of these excuses is detected influencing the review judgment, STOP and recalibrate.
13	
14	| 藉口 (Agent 會說的) | 反駁 (Skill 內建的) |
15	|---------------------|---------------------|
16	| "能跑就夠了" | 能跑但不可讀/不安全/架構錯誤的程式產生複利債務。Review 就是品質關卡。 |
17	| "只是小改動不用審" | 歷史上的重大事故中，60% 來自於被跳過審查的「小改動」。 |
18	| "我寫的我知道它是對的" | 作者對自己的假設有盲點。每段程式都需要另一雙眼睛。 |
19	| "AI 生成的應該沒問題" | AI 程式需要更多審查，不是更少。它自信且 plausible，但可能是錯的。 |
20	| "測試有過就好" | 測試必要但不充分。測試不抓架構問題、安全漏洞、可讀性問題。 |
21	| "以後再整理" | 「以後」永遠不會來。Review 就是品質關卡 — 現在就要求清理。 |
22	| "Review 太花時間" | 未 review 的 bug 修復成本是 review 時發現的 10 倍。 |
23	
24	## Severity Classification
25	
26	Every finding in the review report MUST be tagged with a severity level. Use the following classification:
27	
28	| 等級 | 標記 | 定義 | 範例 |
29	|------|------|------|------|
30	| **Critical** | 🔴 | 必須修復才能 approve | 安全漏洞、資料遺失風險、核心功能損壞 |
31	| **Important** | 🟡 | 應修復或明確討論後才能 approve | 缺少測試、錯誤處理不佳、不符合 spec |
32	| **Suggestion** | 🔵 | 建議改善，非必要 | 命名優化、可選重構、更好的抽象 |
33	| **Nit** | ⚪ | 格式/風格偏好，可忽略 | 空格、換行、個人偏好 |
34	| **FYI** | ℹ️ | 資訊性，無需行動 | 未來注意事項、背景說明 |
35	
36	When in doubt between two levels, choose the HIGHER severity.
37	
38	## 1. Code Quality Review
39	
40	- Read all files produced by this group (from the child issue Rich Summary's file table)
41	- Check: code structure, obvious bugs or anti-patterns, naming and style consistency
42	- Produce: a short comment per file with severity-tagged status
43	
44	## 2. Spec Verification
45	
46	- Read `specs/<capability>/spec.md` from the change directory
47	- If no specs exist: note "No spec found for this group", skip
48	- Check each Requirement against the actual implementation
49	- Produce: coverage status per requirement with severity tag for gaps
50	
51	## 3. Functional Verification
52	
53	Detect project type and gather evidence. All detection is best-effort, skip gracefully.
54	
55	- **Test infrastructure**: Check for `tests/` + `pytest.ini` / `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.pytest]`. If found: run `python -m pytest`, capture output.
56	- **UI**: Check for `.html`, `.tsx`, `.vue`, `.jsx`. If found: use Playwright to screenshot. Upload to GitLab: `glab api --method POST "projects/:id/uploads" -F "file=@screenshot.png"`
57	- **CLI**: Check for CLI entry points in `pyproject.toml` `[project.scripts]`. If found: run basic commands, capture output.
58	- **Fallback**: Try importing or executing the core function.
59	
60	## 4. Architecture Check
61	
62	Review the implementation against system design principles.
63	
64	**Check items**:
65	- Does the change follow existing design patterns? If a new pattern is introduced, is it intentional and documented?
66	- Are module boundaries clean? No circular dependencies?
67	- Is the abstraction level appropriate? (Not too high, not too low — testable and composable)
68	- Are newly introduced dependencies necessary and justified?
69	
70	**Produce**: Status per check item with severity tag for any violations.
71	
72	## 5. Performance Check
73	
74	Identify common performance anti-patterns in the implementation.
75	
76	**Check items**:
77	- Data access: Any N+1 query patterns? (Check for queries inside loops)
78	- API endpoints: Any list endpoints missing pagination?
79	- Async/Sync: Any operations that should be asynchronous but are synchronous?
80	- Frontend: Any unnecessary re-renders? (React: missing useMemo/useCallback; check render-triggering state changes)
81	- Memory/CPU: Any unbounded loops or potential memory leaks? (Missing cleanup in useEffect, unclosed streams)
82	
83	**Produce**: Status per check item with severity tag for any findings.
84	
85	> **Core principle**: Measure before optimizing. Flag patterns, do not prescribe specific optimizations without benchmark data.
86	
87	## 6. Security & Performance Deep Checks
88	
89	For detailed security and performance checks, also read and follow these reference files if they exist in the review skill's references directory:
90	
91	- `references/security-checklist.md` — Security-specific checks (always-check items and red flags)
